To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a hybrid classifier that combines human reasoning with machine learning is more accurate than a pure machine-learning based classifier, and that this hybrid classifier also reduces the human effort required for a given level of classification accuracy.

(i) the hybrid text classifier results in significant improvement of the classification accuracy over machine-learning classifiers when the amount of labeled data available for training is comparable, and that (ii) it also allows for a significant reduction in the human effort required for labeling data.

the human effort required for text classification can be significantly reduced, while maintaining the classification accuracy, by using human reasoning over automatically generated text patterns to complement a machine-learning based classifier.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of techniques that can reduce the human effort in text processing, while retaining the high accuracy of the resulting classifiers.
the development of a hybrid text classifier that combines the strengths of both knowledge-based and data-driven approaches to text categorization.
the problem of how to reduce the human overhead in supervised text classification.

the hybrid approach can reduce the amount of labeled data required by 10x and improve accuracy by 20-30% when compared to machine-learning based approaches.
our hybrid classifier is more accurate than the machine learning classifier, while requiring significantly less labeled data.
this work presents a novel and promising approach to reduce the human overhead in the context of text classification.

the proposed approach is a novel hybrid technique that can be applied to many applications in text processing.
we are able to reduce the human overhead in a text categorization problem by a factor of 5, and at the same time, boost the accuracy by a factor of two.

, by using human reasoning, we can significantly reduce the human effort required in text classification.
, when the goal is to build a text classifier, human reasoning over automatically generated text patterns is more efficient than labeling data.
